blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Preface

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Dear Students,

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Welcome to the tenth standard!

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
This year you will study two text books - Mathematics Part-I and
Mathematics Part-II

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
The main areas in the book Mathematics Part-I are Algebra, Graph,
Financial planning and Statistics. All of these topics were introduced in the
ninth standard. This year you will study some more details of the same. The
new tax system, GST is introduced in Financial planning. Wherever a new
unit, formula or application is introduced, its lucid explanation is given. Each
chapter contains illustrative solved examples and sets of questions for practice.
In addition, some questions in practice sets are star-marked, indicating
that they are challenging for talented students. After tenth standard, some
students do not opt for Mathematics. This book gives them basic concepts
and mathematics needed to work in other fields. The matter under the
head ‘For more information’ is useful for those students who wish to study
mathematics after tenth standard and achieve proficiency in it. So they are
earnestly advised to study it. Read the book thoroughly at least once and
understand the concepts.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Additional useful audio-visual material regarding each lesson will be
available to you by using Q.R. code through ‘App’. It will definitely be
useful to you for your studies.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Much importance is given to the tenth standard examination. You are
advised not to take the stress and study to the best of your ability to achieve
expected success. Best wishes for it !

2. Bear a two- digit number in mind. Without disclosing it, cunstruct a puzzle.

[The above practical can be extended to a three-digit number also.]

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Linear equation in two variables

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
An equation which contains two variables and the degree of each term
containing variable is one, is called a linear equation in two variables.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
$ax + by + c = 0$ is the general form of a linear equation in two variables;
$a, b, c$ are real numbers and $a, b$ are not equal to zero at the same time.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Ex. $3x - 4y + 12 = 0$ is the general form of equation $3x = 4y - 12$

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Simultaneous linear equations

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
When we think about two linear equations in two variables at the same
time, they are called simultaneous equations.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Last year we learnt to solve simultaneous equations by eliminating one
variable. Let us revise it.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex. (1)} Solve the following simultaneous equations.
(1) $5x - 3y = 8$; $3x + y = 2$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Solution :

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
**Method I :** $5x - 3y = 8 \dots$ (I)
$3x + y = 2 \dots$ (II)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Multiplying both sides of
equation (II) by 3.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$ 9x + 3y = 6 . . . \quad \text{(III)} $$
$$ 5x - 3y = 8 . . . \quad \text{(I)} $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Now let us add equations (I)
and (III)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$
\begin{array}{r@{\quad}l}
5x - 3y & = 8 \\
+ 9x + 3y & = 6 \\
\hline
14x & = 14
\end{array}
$$

$$
\therefore x = 1
$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: substituting $x = 1$ in equation (II)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$3x + y = 2$$
$$\therefore 3 \times 1 + y = 2$$
$$\therefore 3 + y = 2$$
$$\therefore \quad y = -1$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
solution is $x = 1$, $y = -1$; it is also
written as $(x, y) = (1, -1)$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Method (II)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$5x - 3y = 8 \dots \text{ (I)}$$
$$3x + y = 2 \dots \text{ (II)}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Let us write value of $y$ in terms
of $x$ from equation (II) as

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$y = 2 - 3x \dots \text{ (III)}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Substituting this value of $y$ in
equation (I).

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$5x - 3y = 8$$
$$\therefore 5x - 3(2 - 3x) = 8$$
$$\therefore 5x - 6 + 9x = 8$$
$$\therefore 14x - 6 = 8$$
$$\therefore 14x = 8 + 6$$
$$\therefore 14x = 14$$
$$\therefore \quad x = 1$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Substituting $x = 1$ in equation
(III).

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$y = 2 - 3x$$
$$\therefore y = 2 - 3 \times 1$$
$$\therefore y = 2 - 3$$
$$\therefore y = -1$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $$x = 1, y = -1 \text{ is the solution.}$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex. (2)} Solve : $3x + 2y = 29$; $5x - y = 18$

\textbf{Solution} : $3x + 2y = 29$ . . . (I) and $5x - y = 18$ . . . (II)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Let's solve the equations by eliminating '$y$'. Fill suitably the boxes below.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Multiplying equation (II) by 2.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore 5x \times \square - y \times \square = 18 \times \square $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore 10x - 2y = \text{______} . . . \text{ (III)} $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Let's add equations (I) and (III)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$3x + 2y = 29$$
$$+ \quad \text{□} - \text{□} = \text{□}$$
$$\overline{\text{□} = \text{□}} \qquad \therefore x = \text{□}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Substituting $x = 5$ in equation (I)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$3x + 2y = 29$
$\therefore 3 \times \square + 2y = 29$
$\therefore \square + 2y = 29$
$\therefore 2y = 29 - \square$
$\therefore 2y = \square \quad \therefore y = \square$
$(x, y) = (\square, \square)$ is the solution.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $(x, y) = (\square, \square)$ is the solution.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: \textbf{Solution} : $15x + 17y = 21$. . . (I)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In the two equations above, the coefficients of $x$ and $y$ are interchanged.
While solving such equations we get two simple equations by adding and
subtracting the given equations. After solving these equations, we can easily find
the solution.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Let's add the two given equations.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Dividing both sides of the equation by 32.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$x + y = 1 \dots \text{ (III)}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Now, let's subtract equation (II) from (I)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$
\begin{array}{r@{\quad}l}
15x + 17y & = 21 \\
-17x \pm 15y & = \underline{-11} \\
\hline
-2x + 2y & = 10
\end{array}
$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: dividing the equation by 2.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ -x + y = 5 \dots \text{ (IV)} $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Now let's add equations (III) and (V).

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$
\begin{array}{r@{\quad}l}
x + y & = 1 \\
+ -x + y & = 5 \\
\hline
\therefore \quad 2y & = 6 \quad \quad \therefore \quad y = 3
\end{array}
$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Place this value in equation (III).

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$x + y = 1$$
$$\therefore x + 3 = 1$$
$$\therefore x = 1 - 3 \qquad \therefore x = -2$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $(x, y) = (-2, 3)$ is the solution.

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Graph of a linear equation in two variables

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In the $9^{\text{th}}$ standard we learnt that the graph of a linear equation in two
variables is a straight line. The ordered pair which satisfies the equation is a
solution of that equation. The ordered pair represents a point on that line.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Ex. Draw graph of $2x - y = 4$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: \textbf{Solution} : To draw a graph of the equation let's write 4 ordered pairs.

blocks.label: Table
blocks.text:
x 0 2 3 -1
y -4 0 2 -6
(x, y) (0, -4) (2, 0) (3, 2) (-1, -6)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
To obtain ordered pair by
simple way let's take $x = 0$
and then $y = 0$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Scale : on both axes
1 cm = 1 unit.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Steps to follow for drawing a graph
of linear equation in two variables.

blocks.label: Infobox
blocks.text:
Two points are sufficient to
represent a line, but if co-ordinates
of one of the two points are
wrong then you will not get a
correct line.
If you plot three points and if
they are non collinear then it is
understood that one of the points
is wrongly plotted. But it is not
easy to identify the incorrect
point.
If we plot four points, it is almost
certain that three of them will be
collinear.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
A linear equation $y = 2$ is also written as $0x + y = 2$. The graph of this
line is parallel to X- axis; as for any value of $x$, $y$ is always 2.

blocks.label: Table
blocks.text:
x 1 4 -3
y 2 2 2
(x, y) (1, 2) (4, 2) (-3, 2)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Similarly equation $x = 2$ is written as $x + 0y = 2$ and its graph is
parallel to Y-axis.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Let's learn.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Graphical method

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: \textbf{Ex.} Let's draw graphs of $x + y = 4$, $2x - y = 2$ and observe them.

blocks.label: Table
blocks.text:
$x$ -1 4 1 6
$y$ 5 0 3 -2
$(x,y)$ (-1,5) (4,0) (1,3) (6,-2)

blocks.label: Table
blocks.text:
x 0 1 3 -1
y -2 0 4 -4
(x, y) (0, -2) (1, 0) (3, 4) (-1, -4)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Hence ordered pair $(2, 2)$
i.e. $x = 2$, $y = 2$ satisfies
the equations $x + y = 4$
and $2x - y = 2$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Each point on the graph
satisfies the equation. The
two lines intersect each
other at $(2, 2)$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
The values of variables that
satisfy the given equations,
give the solution of given
equations.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
$\therefore$ the solution of given
equations $x + y = 4$,
$2x - y = 2$ is $x = 2$,
$y = 2$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Let's solve these equations by method of elimination.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$x + y = 4 \dots (I)$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$2x - y = 2 \dots \text{ (II)}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Adding equations (I) and (II) we
get,

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$3x = 6 \quad \therefore \quad x = 2$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: substituting this value in equation (I)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$x + y = 4$$
$$\therefore 2 + y = 4$$
$$\therefore y = 2$$

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Determinant

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix}$ is a determinant. $(a, b)$, $(c, d)$ are rows and $\begin{pmatrix} a \\ c \end{pmatrix}$, $\begin{pmatrix} b \\ d \end{pmatrix}$
are columns.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Degree of this determinant is 2, because there are 2 elements in each column
and 2 elements in each row. Determinant represents a number which is $(ad-bc)$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: i.e. $\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix} = ad-bc$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $ad-bc$ is the value of determinant $\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix}$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Determinants, usually, are represented with capital letters as
A, B, C, D, . . . . . etc.

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Determinant method (Cramer's Rule)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Using determinants, simultaneous equaions can be solved easily and in less
space. This method is known as determinant method. This method was first
given by a Swiss mathematician Gabriel Cramer, so it is also known as Cram-
er's method.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
To use Cramer's method, the equations are written as $a_1x + b_1y = c_1$ and
$$a_2x + b_2y = c_2.$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1 \dots (I)$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2 \dots \text{ (II)}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Here $x$ and $y$ are variables, $a_1$, $b_1$, $c_1$ and $a_2$, $b_2$, $c_2$ are real numbers,
$$a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1 \neq 0$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Now let us solve these equations.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Multiplying equation (I) by $b_2$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$a_1 b_2 x + b_1 b_2 y = c_1 b_2 \dots \text{(III)}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Multiplying equation (II) by $b_1$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$a_2 b_1 x + b_2 b_1 y = c_2 b_1 \dots \text{(IV)}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Subtracting equation (IV) from (III)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: To remember and write the expressions

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $c_1 b_2 - c_2 b_1, \quad a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1, \quad a_1 c_2 - a_2 c_1 \quad$ we use the determinants.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Now $a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1$ We can write 3 columns. $\begin{pmatrix} a_1 \\ a_2 \end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{pmatrix}$
and $a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
The values $x$, $y$ in equation (V), (VI) are written using determinants as
follows

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$x = \frac{c_1 b_2 - c_2 b_1}{a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1} = \frac{\begin{vmatrix} c_1 & b_1 \\ c_2 & b_2 \end{vmatrix}}{\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 \end{vmatrix}},$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$y = \frac{a_1 c_2 - a_2 c_1}{a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1} = \frac{\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & c_2 \end{vmatrix}}{\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 \end{vmatrix}}$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
To remember let us denote $D = \begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 \end{vmatrix}$, $D_x = \begin{vmatrix} c_1 & b_1 \\ c_2 & b_2 \end{vmatrix}$, $D_y = \begin{vmatrix} a_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & c_2 \end{vmatrix}$
$\therefore x = \frac{D_x}{D}$, $y = \frac{D_y}{D}$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: For writting D, $Dx$, $Dy$ remember the order of columns $\begin{pmatrix} a_1 \\ a_2 \end{pmatrix}$, $\begin{pmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \end{pmatrix}$, $\begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{pmatrix}$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: From the equations,

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$ a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1 $$
and $a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2$ we get the columns $\begin{pmatrix} a_1 \\ a_2 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \begin{pmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{pmatrix}.$

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
$\bullet$ In D the column of constants $\begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{pmatrix}$ is omitted.


$\bullet$ In $D_x$ the column of the coefficients of $x$, $\begin{pmatrix} a_1 \\ a_2 \end{pmatrix}$ is replaced by $\begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{pmatrix}$.


$\bullet$ In $D_y$ the column of the coefficients of $y$, $\begin{pmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \end{pmatrix}$ is replaced by $\begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{pmatrix}$.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex. (1)} Solve the following simultaneous equations using Cramer's Rule.
$$5x + 3y = -11 \ ; \ 2x + 4y = -10$$
\textbf{Solution :} Given equations
$$5x + 3y = -11$$
$$2x + 4y = -10$$
$$D = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{vmatrix} \quad = (5 \times 4) - (2 \times 3) = 20 - 6 = 14$$
$$D_x = \begin{vmatrix} -11 & 3 \\ -10 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = (-11) \times 4 - (-10) \times 3 = -44 \ -(-30)$$
$$= -44 + 30 = -14$$
$$D_y = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & -11 \\ 2 & -10 \end{vmatrix} = 5 \times (-10) - 2 \times (-11) = -50 \ -(-22)$$
$$= -50 + 22 = -28$$
$$x = \frac{D_x}{D} = \frac{-14}{14} = -1 \quad \text{and} \quad y = \frac{D_y}{D} = \frac{-28}{14} = -2$$
$$\therefore (x, y) = (-1, -2) \text{ is the solution.}$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Ex. (1) $\frac{4}{x} + \frac{5}{y} = 7$; $\frac{3}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = 5$
Solution : $\frac{4}{x} + \frac{5}{y} = 7$; $\frac{3}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = 5$
$$4\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) + 5\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 7 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(I)}$$
$$3\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) + 4\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 5 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(II)}$$
Replacing $\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)$ by $m$ and $\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$ by $n$ in equations (I) and (II), we get
$$4m + 5n = 7 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(III)}$$
$$3m + 4n = 5 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(IV)}$$
On solving these equations we get
$m = 3, \ n = -1$
Now, $m = \frac{1}{x} \quad \therefore \ 3 = \frac{1}{x} \quad \therefore \ x = \frac{1}{3}$
$$n = \frac{1}{y} \quad \therefore \ -1 = \frac{1}{y} \quad \therefore \ y = -1$$
$\therefore$ Solution of given simultaneous equations is $(x, y) = \left(\frac{1}{3}, -1\right)$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex.(2)} $\frac{4}{x-y} + \frac{1}{x+y} = 3$ ; $\frac{2}{x-y} - \frac{3}{x+y} = 5$

\textbf{Solution :} $\frac{4}{x-y} + \frac{1}{x+y} = 3$ ; $\frac{2}{x-y} - \frac{3}{x+y} = 5$

$$4\left(\frac{1}{x-y}\right) + 1\left(\frac{1}{x+y}\right) = 3 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(I)}$$

$$2\left(\frac{1}{x-y}\right) - 3\left(\frac{1}{x+y}\right) = 5 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(II)}$$

Replacing $\left(\frac{1}{x-y}\right)$ by $a$ and $\left(\frac{1}{x+y}\right)$ by $b$ we get

$$4a + b = 3 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(III)}$$

$$2a - 3b = 5 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(IV)}$$

On solving these equations we get, $a = 1$ $b = -1$

But $a = \left(\frac{1}{x-y}\right)$ , $b = \left(\frac{1}{x+y}\right)$

$$\therefore \left(\frac{1}{x-y}\right) = 1, \left(\frac{1}{x+y}\right) = -1$$

$$\therefore \quad x - y = 1 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(V)}$$

$$x + y = -1 \ . \ . \ . \quad \text{(VI)}$$

Solving equation (V) and (VI) we get $x = 0, y = -1$

$\therefore$ Solution of the given equations is $(x, y) = (0, -1)$

blocks.text: $\therefore$ Solution of the given equations is $(x, y) = (0, -1)$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex. (1)} The perimeter of a rectangle is 40 cm. The length of the rectangle is
more than double its breadth by 2. Find length and breadth.

\textbf{Solution :} Let length of rectangle be $x$ cm and breadth be $y$ cm.

From first condition -

$$2(x + y) = 40$$

$$x + y = 20 . . . \quad \text{(I)}$$

From $2^{\text{nd}}$ condition -

$$x = 2y + 2$$

$$\therefore x - 2y = 2 . . . \quad \text{(II)}$$

Let's solve eq. (I), (II) by determinant method

$$x + y = 20$$

$$x - 2y = 2$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = [1 \times (-2)] - (1 \times 1) = -2 - 1 = -3 $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \mathrm{D}_{\mathcal{X}} = \begin{vmatrix} 20 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = [20 \times (-2)] - (1 \times 2) = -40 \ -2 = -42 $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 20 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = (1 \times 2) - (20 \times 1) = 2 - 20 = -18 $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$x = \frac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} \text{ and } y = \frac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}}$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore x = \frac{-42}{-3} \text{ and } y = \frac{-18}{-3} $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore x = 14, \quad y = 6 $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ Length of the rectangle is $14$ cm and breadth is $6$ cm.

blocks.text:
A boat travels 16 km upstream
and 24 km downstream in 6
hours.

blocks.label: Infobox
blocks.text:
The same boat travels 36 km
upstream and 48 km downstream
in 13 hours.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Find the speed of water current and speed of boat in still water.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
**Solution :** Let the speed of the boat in still water be $x$ km/hr and the speed
of water current be $y$ km/hr

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore$ speed of boat in downstream $= (x + y)$ km/hr.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: and that in upstream $= (x - y)$ km/hr.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \text{Now distance} = \text{speed} \times \text{time} \qquad \therefore \text{time} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Time taken by the boat to travel 16 km upstream = $\frac{16}{x-y}$ hours and it
takes $\frac{24}{x+y}$ hours to travel 24 km downstream.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: from first condition -

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: from $2^{\text{nd}}$ condition

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \frac{36}{x-y} + \frac{48}{x+y} = 13 \dots \text{ (II)} $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: By replacing $\frac{1}{x-y}$ by $m$ and $\frac{1}{x+y}$ by $n$ we get

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$16m + 24n = 6 \dots \text{ (III)}$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$36m + 48n = 13 \dots \text{ (IV)}$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Solving equations (III) and (IV) $m = \frac{1}{4}$, $n = \frac{1}{12}$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Repalcing $m$, $n$ by their original values we get

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$x - y = 4 \dots \quad (V) \quad x + y = 12 \dots \quad (VI)$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Solving equations (V), (VI) we get $x = 8$, $y = 4$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
$\therefore$ speed of the boat in still water is 8 km/hr. and speed of water current
is 4 km/hr.

blocks.text:
**Ex.** (4) A certain amount is equally distributed among certain number of students.
Each would get $₹ 2$ less if 10 students were more and each would get
$₹ 6$ more if 15 students were less. Find the number of students and the
amount distributed.

blocks.label: Answer
blocks.text:
\textbf{Solution :} Let the number of students be $x$ and amount given to each student
be \text{\textasciicircum} $y$.
$\therefore$ Total amount distributed is $xy$
From the first condition we get,
$(x + 10) (y - 2) = xy$
$\therefore xy - 2x + 10y - 20 = xy$
$\therefore - 2x + 10y = 20$
$\therefore - x + 5y = 10 . . . \quad (\text{I})$
From the $2^{\text{nd}}$ condition we get,
$(x - 15) (y + 6) = xy$
$\therefore xy + 6x - 15y - 90 = xy$
$\therefore 6x - 15y = 90$
$\therefore 2x - 5y = 30 . . . \quad (\text{II})$
Adding equations (I) and (II)
$- x + 5y = 10$
$+ \quad 2x - 5y = 30$
\rule{13cm}{0.4pt}
$x = 40$
Substitute this value of $x$ in equation (I)
$- x + 5y = 10$
$\therefore - 40 + 5y = 10$
$\therefore \quad 5y = 50$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore \quad y = 10 $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Total amount distributed is $= xy = 40 \times 10 = \text{₹ } 400.$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ ₹ 400 distributed equally among 40 students.

blocks.text:
**Ex. (5)** A three digit number is equal to 17 times the sum of its digits; If the digits are
reversed, the new number is 198 more than the old number ; also the sum of
extreme digits is less than the middle digit by unity. Find the original number.
**Solution :** Let the digit in hundreds place be $x$ and that in unit place be $y$.

| H | T | unit |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| $x$ | $x + y + 1$ | $y$ |

$\therefore$ the three digit number is $100x + 10(x + y + 1) + y$
$= 100x + 10x + 10y + 10 + y = 110x + 11y + 10$
the sum of the digits in the given number $= x + (x + y + 1) + y = 2x + 2y + 1$
$\therefore$ From first condition
Given number $= 17 \times$ (sum of the digits)
$\therefore 110x + 11y + 10 = 17 \times (2x + 2y + 1)$
$\therefore 110x + 11y + 10 = 34x + 34y + 17$
$\therefore 76x - 23y = 7 \dots$ (I)
The number obtained by reversing the digits
$= 100y + 10(x + y + 1) + x = 110y + 11x + 10$
Given number $= 110x + 11y + 10$
From $2^{\text{nd}}$ condition, Given number $+ 198 =$ new number.
$110x + 11y + 10 + 198 = 110y + 11x + 10$
$99x - 99y = -198$
$x - y = -2$
$\therefore x = y - 2 \dots$ (II)
Substitute this value of $x$ in equation (I).
$\therefore 76(y - 2) - 23y = 7$
$\therefore 76y - 152 - 23y = 7$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \quad y = 3 \quad \therefore$ the digit in units place is $= 3$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Substitute this value in equation (II)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore \quad x = 3 - 2 = 1 $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \quad x = 1 \quad \therefore$ The digit in hundred's place is 1

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: the digit in ten's place is $3 + 1 + 1 = 5$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore$ the number is $153$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
The equation involving one variable with all indices as whole numbers and having
2 as the maximum index of the variable is called the quadratic equation.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: General form is $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, $a, b, c$ are real numbers and $a \neq 0$.
$ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ is the general form of quadratic equation.

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Roots of a quadratic equation

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In the previous class you have studied that if value of the polynomial is zero for
$x = a$ then $(x - a)$ is a factor of that polynomial. That is if $\mathrm{p}(x)$ is a polynomial and
$\mathrm{p}(a) = 0$ then $(x - a)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{p}(x)$. In this case '$a$' is the root or solution of $\mathrm{p}(x) = 0$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: For Example ,

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Let $x = -6$ in the polynomial $x^2 + 5x - 6$
$$x^2 + 5x - 6 = (-6)^2 + 5 \times (-6) - 6$$
$$= 36 - 30 - 6 = 0$$
$\therefore x = -6$ is a solution of the equation.
Hence $-6$ is one root of the equation
$$x^2 + 5x - 6 = 0$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
Let $x = 2$ in polynomial $x^2 + 5x - 6$
$$x^2 + 5x - 6 = 2^2 + 5 \times 2 - 6$$
$$= 4 + 10 - 6$$
$$= 8 \neq 0$$
$\therefore \quad x = 2$ is not a solution of the
equation $x^2 + 5x - 6 = 0$

blocks.text: Solved Example

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex.} $2x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0$ check whether (i) $x = \frac{3}{2}$ , (ii) $x = -2$ are solutions of the equations.
\textbf{Solution :} (i) Put $x = \frac{3}{2}$ in the polynomial $2x^2 - 7x + 6$
$$2x^2 - 7x + 6 = 2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 - 7\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) + 6$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore x = \frac{3}{2}$ is a solution of the equation.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore x = -2$ is not a solution of the equation.

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Solutions of a quadratic equation by factorisation

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
By substituting arbitrary values for the variable and deciding the roots of quadratic
equation is a time consuming process. Let us learn to use factorisation method to find
the roots of the given quadratic equation.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $(x - 5)$ and $(x + 1)$ are two linear factors of quadratic polynomial $x^2 - 4 x - 5$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
So the quadratic equation obtained from $x^2 - 4 x - 5$ can be written as
$$(x - 5) (x + 1) = 0$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: If product of two numbers is zero then at least one of them is zero.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \quad x - 5 = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad x + 1 = 0$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \quad x = 5 \text{ or } x = -1$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ 5 and the $-1$ are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
While solving the equation first we obtained the linear factors. So we call this
method as 'factorization method' of solving quadratic equation.

(1) $m^2 - 14 m + 13 = 0$

$\therefore m^2 - 13 m - 1m + 13 = 0$      (2) $3x^2 - x - 10 = 0$

$\therefore \overline{m (m - 13)} \overline{-1 (m - 13)} = 0$      $\therefore \underline{3x^2 - 6x} + \underline{5x - 10} = 0$

$\therefore (m - 13) (m - 1) = 0$      $\therefore 3x (x - 2) + 5 (x - 2) = 0$

$\therefore m - 13 = 0$ or $m - 1 = 0$      $\therefore (3x + 5) (x - 2) = 0$

$\therefore m = 13$ or $m = 1$      $\therefore (3x + 5) = 0$ or $(x - 2) = 0$

$\therefore 13$ and $1$ are the roots of the given      $\therefore x = -\frac{5}{3}$ or $x = 2$

quadratic equation.      quadratic equation.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
(3) $3y^2 = 15 y$
$\therefore 3y^2 - 15 y = 0$
$\therefore 3y (y - 5) = 0$
$\therefore 3y = 0 \text{ or } (y - 5) = 0$
$\therefore y = 0 \text{ or } y = 5$
$\therefore 0 \text{ and } 5 \text{ are the roots of quadratic}$
equation.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
(4) $x^2 = 3$

$\therefore x^2 - 3 = 0$

$\therefore x^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2 = 0$

$\therefore (x + \sqrt{3}) (x - \sqrt{3}) = 0$

$\therefore (x + \sqrt{3}) = 0 \text{ or } (x - \sqrt{3}) = 0$

$\therefore x = -\sqrt{3} \text{ or } x = \sqrt{3}$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
$\therefore -\sqrt{3}$ and $\sqrt{3}$ are the roots of given
quadratic equation.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
(5) $6\sqrt{3}x^2 + 7x = \sqrt{3}$

$\therefore 6\sqrt{3}x^2 + 7x - \sqrt{3} = 0$

$\therefore 6\sqrt{3}x^2 + 9x - 2x - \sqrt{3} = 0$

$\therefore 3\sqrt{3}x(2x + \sqrt{3}) - 1(2x + \sqrt{3}) = 0$

$\therefore (2x + \sqrt{3})(3\sqrt{3}x - 1) = 0$

$\therefore 2x + \sqrt{3} = 0$ or $3\sqrt{3}x - 1 = 0$

$\therefore 2x = -\sqrt{3}$ or $3\sqrt{3}x = 1$

$\therefore x = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ or $x = \frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}$

$\therefore -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}$ are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

blocks.text: Solution of a quadratic equation by completing the square

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Teacher : Is $x^2 + 10 x + 2 = 0$ a quadratic equation or not ?

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Yogesh : Yes Sir, because it is in the form $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, maximum index of the
variable $x$ is 2 and '$a$' is non zero.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Teacher : Can you solve this equation ?

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Yogesh : No Sir, because it is not possible to find the factors of 2 whose sum is 10.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Teacher : Right, so we have to use another method to solve such equations. Let us
learn the method.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Let us add a suitable term to $x^2 + 10 x$ so that the new expression would be a
complete square.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: then $x^2 + 10 x + k = x^2 + 2ax + a^2$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore 10 = 2a$ and $k = a^2$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: by equating the coefficients for the variable $x$ and constant term

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore a = 5 \quad \therefore \quad k = a^2 = (5)^2 = 25$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Now can you solve the equation $x^2 + 10 x + 2 = 0$ ?

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Rehana : Yes Sir, left side of the equation is now difference of two squares and we
can factorise it.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$(x + 5)^2 - (\sqrt{23})^2 = 0$$
$$\therefore (x + 5 + \sqrt{23})(x + 5 - \sqrt{23}) = 0$$
$$\therefore x + 5 + \sqrt{23} = 0 \text{ or } x + 5 - \sqrt{23} = 0$$
$$\therefore x = -5 - \sqrt{23} \text{ or } x = -5 + \sqrt{23}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Hameed : Sir, May I suggest another way ?

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$(x + 5)^2 - (\sqrt{23})^2 = 0$$
$$\therefore (x + 5)^2 = (\sqrt{23})^2$$
$$\therefore x + 5 = \sqrt{23} \text{ or } x + 5 = -\sqrt{23}$$
$$\therefore x = -5 + \sqrt{23} \text{ or } x = -5 - \sqrt{23}$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (1) Solve :** $5x^2 - 4x - 3 = 0$

**Solution :** It is convenient to make coefficient of $x^2$ as 1 and then convert the equation

as the of difference of two squares, so dividing the equation by 5,

we get, $x^2 - \frac{4}{5} x - \frac{3}{5} = 0$

now if $x^2 - \frac{4}{5} x + k = (x - a)^2$ then $x^2 - \frac{4}{5} x + k = x^2 - 2ax + a^2$.

compare the terms in $x^2 - \frac{4}{5} x$ and $x^2 - 2ax$.

$- 2 ax = - \frac{4}{5} x \quad \therefore a = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{2}{5}$

$\therefore k = a^2 = \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{25}$

Now, $x^2 - \frac{4}{5} x - \frac{3}{5} = 0$

$\therefore x^2 - \frac{4}{5} x + \frac{4}{25} - \frac{4}{25} - \frac{3}{5} = 0$

$\therefore \left(x - \frac{2}{5}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{4}{25} + \frac{3}{5}\right) = 0$

$\therefore \left(x - \frac{2}{5}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{19}{25}\right) = 0$

$\therefore \left(x - \frac{2}{5}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{19}{25}\right)$

$\therefore x - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{\sqrt{19}}{5}$ or $x - \frac{2}{5} = - \frac{\sqrt{19}}{5}$

$\therefore x = \frac{2}{5} + \frac{\sqrt{19}}{5}$ or $x = \frac{2}{5} - \frac{\sqrt{19}}{5}$

$\therefore x = \frac{2 + \sqrt{19}}{5}$ or $x = \frac{2 - \sqrt{19}}{5}$

$\therefore \frac{2 + \sqrt{19}}{5}$ and $\frac{2 - \sqrt{19}}{5}$ are roots of the equation.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Ex. (2) Solve : $x^2 + 8x - 48 = 0$

Method I : Completing the square.

$x^2 + 8x - 48 = 0$

$\therefore x^2 + 8x + 16 - 16 - 48 = 0$

$\therefore (x + 4)^2 - 64 = 0$

$\therefore (x + 4)^2 = 64$

$\therefore x + 4 = 8$ or $x + 4 = -8$

$\therefore x = 4$ or $x = -12$

Method II : Factorisation

$x^2 + 8x - 48 = 0$

$\therefore x^2 + 12x - 4x - 48 = 0$

$\therefore x (x + 12) - 4(x + 12) = 0$

$\therefore (x + 12) (x - 4) = 0$

$\therefore x + 12 = 0$ or $x - 4 = 0$

$\therefore x = -12$ or $x = 4$

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Formula for solving a quadratic equation

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $ax^2 + bx + c$, Divide the polynomial by $a$ ($\because a \neq 0$) to get $x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \frac{c}{a}$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Let us write the polynomial $x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \frac{c}{a}$ in the form of difference of two square
numbers. Now we can obtain roots or solutions of equation $x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \frac{c}{a} = 0$ which is
equivalent to $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ .

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$ax^2 + bx + c = 0 \dots$ (I)

$x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \frac{c}{a} = 0 \dots$ dividing both sides by $a$

$\therefore x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \left(\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \frac{c}{a} = 0$

$\therefore \left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - \frac{b^2}{4a^2} + \frac{c}{a} = 0$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore \left( x + \frac{b}{2a} \right)^2 - \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2} = 0 \qquad \therefore \left( x + \frac{b}{2a} \right)^2 = \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2} $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore x + \frac{b}{2a} = \sqrt{\frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2}} \text{ or } x + \frac{b}{2a} = -\sqrt{\frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2}} $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore \quad x = -\frac{b}{2a} + \sqrt{\frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2}} \quad \text{or} \quad x = -\frac{b}{2a} - \sqrt{\frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2}} $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$\therefore x = \frac{-b + \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \text{ or } x = \frac{-b - \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In short the solution is written as $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ and these values are denoted
by $\alpha$, $\beta$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \alpha = \frac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} , \quad \beta = \frac{-b-\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} . . . . . . . . . . . (I)$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
The values of $a, b, c$ from equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ are substituted in
$\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ and further simplified to obtain the roots of the equation. So

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
$$x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \text{ is the formula used to solve quadratic equation. Out of the two}$$
roots any one can be represented by $\alpha$ and the other by $\beta$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: That is, instead (I) we can write $\alpha = \frac{-b-\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$ , $\beta = \frac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$ . . . . (II)

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Note that : If $\alpha = \frac{-b + \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ then $\alpha > \beta$, if $\alpha = \frac{-b - \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ then $\alpha < \beta$

Ex. (1)      $m^2 - 14 m + 13 = 0$
Solution : $m^2 - 14 m + 13 = 0$ comparing
      with $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$
      we get $a = 1, \ b = -14, \ c = 13,$
$\therefore b^2 - 4 ac = (-14)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 13$
      $= 196 - 52$
      $= 144$

$m = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$
$= \frac{(-14) \pm \sqrt{144}}{2 \times 1}$
$= \frac{14 \pm 12}{2}$
$\therefore m = \frac{14 + 12}{2} \text{ or } m = \frac{14 - 12}{2}$
$\therefore m = \frac{26}{2} \text{ or } m = \frac{2}{2}$
$\therefore m = 13 \text{ or } m = 1$
$\therefore 13 \text{ and } 1 \text{ are roots of the equation.}$

**Ex.** (4) $25x^2 + 30x + 9 = 0$

**Solution :** $25x^2 + 30x + 9 = 0$ comparing

the equation with $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$

we get $a = 25$, $b = 30$, $c = 9$,

$\therefore b^2 - 4\ ac = (30)^2 - 4 \times 25 \times 9$

$= 900 - 900 \quad = 0$

$$x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$

$$= \frac{-30 \pm \sqrt{0}}{2 \times 25}$$

$$\therefore \quad x = \frac{-30 + 0}{50} \quad \text{or} \quad x = \frac{-30 - 0}{50}$$

$$\therefore \quad x = -\frac{30}{50} \quad \text{or} \quad x = -\frac{30}{50}$$

$$\therefore \quad x = -\frac{3}{5} \quad \text{or} \quad x = -\frac{3}{5}$$

that is both the roots are equal.

Also note that $25x^2 + 30x + 9 = 0$

means $(5x + 3)^2 = 0$

we get $a = 1$, $b = 1$, $c = 5$,

$$= 1 - 20$$

$$= -19$$

$$x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$

$$= \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{-19}}{2 \times 1}$$

$$= \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{-19}}{2}$$

But $\sqrt{-19}$ is not a real number. Hence

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Nature of roots of a quadratic equation

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: You know that $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ are roots of quadratic equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: (1) If $b^2 - 4ac = 0$ then, $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{0}}{2a} \therefore x = \frac{-b+0}{2a}$ or $x = \frac{-b-0}{2a}$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ the roots of the quadratic equation are real and equal.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: (2) If $b^2 - 4ac > 0$, then $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: i.e. $x = \frac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$ and $x = \frac{-b-\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ roots of the quadratic equation are real and unequal.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
(3) If $b^2 - 4ac < 0$ then $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ are not real numbers $\therefore$ the roots of
quadratic equations are not real.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Nature of roots of quadratic equation is determined by the value of $b^2 - 4ac$.
$b^2 - 4ac$ is called discriminant of a quadratic equation and is denoted by Greek letter
$\Delta$ (Delta)

\textbf{Ex. (3)} $\sqrt{3} x^2 + 2 \sqrt{3} x + \sqrt{3} = 0$

\textbf{Solution :} Compare $\sqrt{3} x^2 + 2 \sqrt{3} x + \sqrt{3} = 0$ with $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$

We get $a = \sqrt{3}$ , $b = 2 \sqrt{3}$ , $c = \sqrt{3}$ ,

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: The relation between roots of the quadratic equation and coefficients

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ then,

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$\alpha + \beta = \frac{-b + \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} + \frac{-b - \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$
$$= \frac{-b + \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac} - b - \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$
$$= - \frac{2b}{2a}$$
$$\therefore \alpha + \beta = - \frac{b}{a}$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$\alpha \times \beta = \frac{-b + \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \times \frac{-b - \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$
$$= \frac{\left(-b + \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}\right) \times \left(-b - \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}\right)}{4a^2}$$
$$= \frac{b^2 - \left(b^2 - 4ac\right)}{4a^2}$$
$$= \frac{4ac}{4a^2}$$
$$= \frac{c}{a}$$
$$\therefore \alpha \beta = \frac{c}{a}$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex. (1)} If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the quadratic equation $2x^2 + 6x - 5 = 0$, then find
$$(\alpha + \beta) \text{ and } \alpha \times \beta.$$
\textbf{Solution :} Comparing $2x^2 + 6x - 5 = 0$ with $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$.
$$\therefore \quad a = 2, \quad b = 6, \quad c = -5$$
$$\therefore \quad \alpha + \beta = -\frac{b}{a} = -\frac{6}{2} = -3$$
$$\text{and } \alpha \times \beta = \frac{c}{a} = \frac{-5}{2}$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
\textbf{Ex. (2)} The difference between the roots of the equation $x^2 - 13x + k = 0$ is 7 find k.
\textbf{Solution :} Comparing $x^2 - 13x + k = 0$ with $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$
$$a = 1, \ b = -13 \ , \ c = k$$
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation.
$$\alpha + \beta = -\frac{b}{a} = -\frac{(-13)}{1} = 13 \dots \text{ (I)}$$
But $\alpha - \beta = 7 \dots \dots \dots \dots \dots \text{ (given) (II)}$
$$2 \alpha = 20 \ \dots \ \text{(adding (I) and (II))}$$
$$\therefore \alpha = 10$$
$$\therefore 10 + \beta = 13 \dots \text{ (from (I))}$$
$$\therefore \beta = 13 - 10$$
$$\therefore \beta = 3$$
But $\alpha \times \beta = \frac{c}{a}$
$$\therefore 10 \times 3 = \frac{k}{1}$$
$$\therefore k = 30$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (3)** If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^2 + 5x - 1 = 0$ then find -

(i) $\alpha^3 + \beta^3$ (ii) $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$.

**Solution :** $x^2 + 5x - 1 = 0$

$$a = 1, \quad b = 5, \quad c = -1$$

$$\alpha + \beta = -\frac{b}{a} = \frac{-5}{1} = -5$$

$$\alpha \times \beta = \frac{c}{a} = \frac{-1}{1} = -1$$

(i) $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha + \beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta (\alpha + \beta)$

$= (-5)^3 - 3 \times (-1) \times (-5)$

$= -125 - 15$

$\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = -140$

(ii) $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta$

$= (-5)^2 - 2 \times (-1)$

$= 25 + 2$

$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 27$

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: To obtain a quadratic equation having given roots

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of a quadratic equation in variable $x$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$\therefore x = \alpha$ or $x = \beta$

$\therefore x - \alpha = 0$ or $x - \beta = 0$

$\therefore (x - \alpha)(x - \beta) = 0$

$\therefore x^2 - (\alpha + \beta) x + \alpha\beta = 0$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
When two roots of equation are given then quadratic equation can be obtained
as $x^2 -$ (addition of roots) $x +$ product of the roots $= 0$.

blocks.text:

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Activity (II) : What will be the quadratic equation if $\alpha = 2, \beta = 5$

It can be written as $x^2 - (\quad + \quad) x + \quad \times \quad = 0.$
that is $\quad x^2 - \quad x + \quad = 0.$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Note that, if this equation is multiplied by any non zero number, the roots of the
equation are not changed.

blocks.text: Solved examples

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex.** Obtain the quadratic equation if roots are $-3, -7$.

**Solution :** Let $\alpha = -3$ and $\beta = -7$

$\therefore \alpha + \beta = (-3) + (-7) = -10$ and $\alpha \times \beta = (-3) \times (-7) = 21$

$\therefore$ and quadratic equation is, $x^2 - (\alpha + \beta) x + \alpha \beta = 0$

$\therefore x^2 - (-10) x + 21 = 0$

$\therefore x^2 + 10x + 21 = 0$

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Let's remember!

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
(1) If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of quadratic equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$,
(i) $\alpha = \frac{-b + \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ and $\beta = \frac{-b - \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$
(ii) $\alpha + \beta = -\frac{b}{a}$ and $\alpha \times \beta = \frac{c}{a}$
(2) Nature of roots of quadratic equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ depends on the value
of $b^2 - 4ac$. Hence $b^2 - 4ac$ is called discriminant and is denoted by Greek
letter $\Delta$.
(3) If $\Delta = 0$ The roots of quadratic equation are real and equal.
If $\Delta > 0$ then the roots of quadratic equation are real and unequal.
If $\Delta < 0$ then the roots of quadratic equation are not real.
(4) The quadratic equation, whose roots are $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is
$$x^2 - (\alpha + \beta) x + \alpha\beta = 0$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Quadratic equations are useful in daily life for finding solutions of some practical
problems. We are now going to learn the same.

**Ex. (1)** There is a rectangular onion storehouse in the farm of Mr. Ratnakarrao at
Tivasa. The length of rectangular base is more than its breadth by $7$ m and diagonal is
more than length by $1$ m. Find length and breadth of the storehouse.

**Solution :** Let breadth of the storehouse be $x$ m.
$\therefore$ length = $(x + 7)$ m, diagonal = $x + 7 + 1$ = $(x + 8)$ m
By Pythagoras theorem
$$x^2 + (x + 7)^2 = (x + 8)^2$$
$$x^2 + x^2 + 14x + 49 = x^2 + 16x + 64$$
$\therefore x^2 + 14x - 16x + 49 - 64 = 0$
$\therefore x^2 - 2x - 15 = 0$
$\therefore \underline{x^2 - 5x + 3x - 15} = 0$
$\therefore x(x - 5) + 3 (x - 5) = 0$
$\therefore (x - 5) (x + 3) = 0$
$\therefore x - 5 = 0$ or $x + 3 = 0$
$\therefore x = 5$ or $x = -3$
But length is never negative $\therefore x \neq -3$
$\therefore x = 5$ and $x + 7 = 5 + 7 = 12$
$\therefore$ Length of the base of storehouse is $12$m and breadth is $5$m.

Onion Storehouse (Kandachal)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ Length of the base of storehouse is $12\text{m}$ and breadth is $5\text{m}$.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (2)** A train travels 360 km with uniform speed.The speed of the train is increased
by 5 km/hr, it takes 48 minutes less to cover the same distance. Find the initial
speed of the train.

**Solution :** Let initial speed of the train be $x$ km/hr.

$\therefore$ New speed is $(x+5)$ km/hr.
time to cover 360 km = $\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} = \frac{360}{x}$ hours.
New time after increasing speed = $\frac{360}{x+5}$ hours.
from given condition

$\frac{360}{x+5} = \frac{360}{x} - \frac{48}{60} \quad \text{--- ( 48 min = } \frac{48}{60} \text{ hrs)}$
$\therefore \frac{360}{x} - \frac{360}{x+5} = \frac{48}{60}$
$\therefore \frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{x+5} = \frac{48}{60 \times 360} \quad \text{--- (Dividing both sides by 360)}$

$\frac{x+5-x}{x(x+5)} = \frac{4}{5 \times 360}$
$\therefore \frac{5}{x^2+5x} = \frac{1}{5 \times 90}$
$\therefore \frac{5}{x^2+5x} = \frac{1}{450}$

$\therefore x^2 + 5x = 2250$
$\therefore x^2 + 5x - 2250 = 0$
$\therefore \underline{x^2 + 50x} - \underline{45x - 2250} = 0 \quad \text{---2250}$
$\therefore \underline{x(x+50)} - \underline{45(x+50)} = 0 \quad \text{---+50 -45}$
$\therefore (x+50)(x-45) = 0$

$\therefore x + 50 = 0 \text{ or } x - 45 = 0$
$\therefore x = -50 \text{ or } x = 45$

But speed is never negative $\therefore x \neq -50$

$\therefore x = 45$

$\therefore$ Initial speed of the train is 45 km/hr.

blocks.text: 3 Arithmetic Progression

blocks.label: Infobox
blocks.text:
Let's study.

* Sequence                                     * $n^{th}$ term of an A.P.
* Arithmetic Progression                       * Sum of n terms of an A.P.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Let's learn.

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Sequence

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
We write numbers $1, 2, 3, 4, \dots$ in an order. In this order we can tell the position
of any number. For example, number $13$ is at $13^{\text{th}}$ position. The numbers $1, 4, 9, 16,$
$25, 36, 49, \dots$ are also written in a particular order. Here $16 = 4^2$ is at $4^{\text{th}}$ position.
similarly, $25 = 5^2$ is at the $5^{\text{th}}$ position; $49 = 7^2$ is at the $7^{\text{th}}$ position. In this set of
numbers also, place of each number is detremined.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
A set of numbers where the numbers are arranged in a definite order, like the
natural numbers, is called a \textbf{sequence}.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In a sequence a particular number is written at a particular position. If the numbers
are written as $a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 \dots$ then $a_1$ is first, $a_2$ is second, $\dots$ and so on. It is clear
that $a_n$ is at the $\text{n}^{\text{th}}$ place. A sequence of the numbers is also represented by alphabets
$f_1, f_2, f_3, \dots$ and we find that there is a definite order in which numbers are arranged.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
When students stand in a row for drill on the playground they form a sequence.
We have experienced that some sequences have a particular pattern.

In general, only those sequences are studied where there is a rule which determines
the next term.

blocks.label: Section-title

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In a sequence, ordered terms are represented as $t_1, t_2, t_3, \dots \dots t_n \dots$ In general
sequence is written as $\{t_n\}$. If the sequence is infinite, for every positive integer $n$,
there is a term $t_n$.

If the difference between two consecutive terms is constant then it is called the

blocks.label: Paragraph

In the given sequence if the difference between two consecutive terms $(t_{n+1} - t_n)$ is
constant then the sequence is called Arithmetic Progression (A.P.). In this sequence
$t_{n+1} - t_n = d$ is the common difference.

Let's remember!

(1) In a sequence if difference $(t_{n+1} - t_n)$ is constant then the sequence
is called an arithmetic progression.
(2) In an A.P. the difference between two consecutive terms is constant
and is denoted by $d$.
(3) Difference $d$ can be positive, negative or zero.
(4) In an A.P. if the first term is $a$, and common difference is $d$ then the
terms in the sequence are $a, (a + d), (a + 2d), \dots$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Ex. (1) Which of the following sequences are A.P ? If it is an A.P, find next two terms.

(i) $5, 12, 19, 26, \dots$      (ii) $2, -2, -6, -10, \dots$

(iii) $1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, \dots$      (iv) $\frac{3}{2}, \frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}, \dots$

Solution : (i) In this sequence $5, 12, 19, 26, \dots$,

First term $= t_1 = 5, \quad t_2 = 12, \quad t_3 = 19, \dots$

$t_2 - t_1 = 12 - 5 = 7$

$t_3 - t_2 = 19 - 12 = 7$

Here first term is $5$ and common difference which is constant is $d = 7$

$\therefore$ This sequence is an A.P.

Next two terms in this A.P. are $26 + 7 = 33$ and $33 + 7 = 40$.

Next two terms in given A.P. are $33$ and $40$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: (ii) In the sequence $2, -2, -6, -10, \dots$,

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: From this difference between two consecutive terms that is $t_n - t_{n-1} = -4$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore d = -4$, which is constant. $\therefore$ It is an A.P.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Next two terms in this A.P. are $(-10) + (-4) = -14$ and $(-14) + (-4) = -18$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: (iii) In the sequence $1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, \dots$,

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$t_1=1, \quad t_2=1, \quad t_3=2, \quad t_4=2, \quad t_5=3, \quad t_6=3 \dots$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: In this sequence difference between two consecutive terms is not constant.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ This sequence is not an A.P.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: (iv) In the sequence $\frac{3}{2}, \frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{3}{2}, \dots,$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$t_1 = \frac{3}{2}, \quad t_2 = \frac{1}{2}, \quad t_3 = -\frac{1}{2}, \quad t_4 = -\frac{3}{2} \dots$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Here the common difference $d = -1$ which is constant.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ Given sequence is an A.P. Let's find next two terms of this A.P.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore$ Next two terms are $-\frac{5}{2}$ and $-\frac{7}{2}$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (1)** Find $t_n$ for following A.P. and then
find $30^{\text{th}}$ term of A.P.

$3, 8, 13, 18, \dots$

**Solution** :Given A.P. $3, 8, 13, 18, \dots$

Here $t_1 = 3, t_2 = 8, t_3 = 13, t_4 = 18, \dots$

$d = t_2 - t_1 = 8 - 3 = 5$

We know that $t_n = a + (n - 1)d$

$\therefore t_n = 3 + (n - 1) \times 5 \quad \because a = 3, d = 5$

$\therefore t_n = 3 + 5n - 5$

$\therefore t_n = 5n - 2$

$\therefore 30^{\text{th}}$ term $= t_{30} = 5 \times 30 - 2$

$= 150 - 2 \quad = 148$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (3) Check whether 301 is in the sequence**

$$5, 11, 17, 23, \dots ?$$

**Solution :** In the sequence $5, 11, 17, 23, \dots$

$$t_1 = 5, \ t_2 = 11, \ t_3 = 17, \ t_4 = 23, \dots$$

$$t_2 - t_1 = 11 - 5 = 6$$

$$t_3 - t_2 = 17 - 11 = 6$$

$$\therefore \text{This sequence is an A.P.}$$

$$\text{First term } a = 5 \text{ and } d = 6$$

$$\text{If 301 is } n^{\text{th}} \text{ term, then.}$$

$$t_n = a + (n - 1)d = 301$$

$$\therefore 301 = 5 + (n - 1) \times 6$$

$$= 5 + 6n - 6$$

$$\therefore 6n = 301 + 1 = 302$$

$$\therefore n = \frac{302}{6} . \text{ But it is not an integer.}$$

$$\therefore 301 \text{ is not in the given sequence.}$$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (2)** Which term of the following A.P.
is 560?

$$2, 11, 20, 29, \dots$$

**Solution :** Given A.P. 2, 11, 20, 29, . .

Here $a=2$, $d=11-2=9$

$n^{\text{th}}$ term of this A.P. is 560.

$t_n = a + (n-1)d$

$\therefore 560 = 2 + (n-1) \times 9$

$= 2 + 9n - 9$

$\therefore 9n = 567$

$\therefore n = \frac{567}{9} = 63$

$\therefore 63^{\text{rd}}$ term of given A.P. is 560.

Ex. (4) How many two digit numbers are
       divisible by 4?
Solution : List of two digit numbers
       divisible by 4 is
       $12, 16, 20, 24, \dots, 96.$
       Let's find how many such numbers
       are there.
       $t_n = 96, \quad a = 12, \quad d = 4$
       From this we will find the value of $n$.
       $t_n = 96, \therefore$ By formula,
       $96 = 12 + (n - 1) \times 4$
       $= 12 + 4n - 4$
$\therefore 4n = 88$
$\therefore n = 22$
$\therefore$ There are 22 two digit numbers
divisible by 4.

\textbf{Ex. (5)} – The $10^{\text{th}}$ term and the $18^{\text{th}}$ term of an A.P. are 25 and 41 respectively then
find $38^{\text{th}}$ term of that A.P., similarly if $n^{\text{th}}$ term is 99. Find the value of $n$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: **Solution :** In the given A.P. $t_{10} = 25$ and $t_{18} = 41$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: We know that, $t_n = a + (n - 1)d$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore \quad t_{10} = a + (10 - 1) d $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \quad 25 = a + 9d \dots \text{ (I)}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Similarly $t_{18} = a + (18 - 1) d$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \quad 41 = a + 17d \dots (\text{II})$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $25 = a + 9d \dots$ From (I).

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Substituting this value in equation II.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$\therefore$ Equation (II) $a + 17d = 41$
$\therefore$ $25 - 9d + 17d = 41$
$8d = 41 - 25 = 16$
$d = 2$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Substituting $d = 2$ in equation I.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text:
$$a + 9d = 25$$
$$\therefore a + 9 \times 2 = 25$$
$$\therefore a + 18 = 25$$
$$\therefore a = 7$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: If $n^{\text{th}}$ term is 99, then to find value of $n$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ In the given progression $38^{\text{th}}$ term is $81$ and $99$ is the $47^{\text{th}}$ term.

Once upon a time, there lived a king. He appointed two teachers Tara and Meera
to teach horse riding  for one year to his children Yashwantraje and Geetadevi. He

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Sum of first n terms of an A. P.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Arithmetic Progression $a, a + d, a + 2d, a + 3d, \dots a +(n - 1)d$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In this progression $a$ is the first term and $d$ is the common difference. Let's write the
sum of first $n$ terms as $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}}$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$S_n = \quad [a] \quad + \quad [a+d] \quad + \dots + [a+(n-2)d] + [a+(n-1)d]$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Reversing the terms and rewriting the expression again,

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$S_n = [a+(n-1)d] \quad + [a+(n-2)d] \quad + \dots + [a+d] + [a]$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: On adding,

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$2S_n = [2a+(n-1)d] \quad + [2a+(n-1)d] \quad + \dots + [2a+(n-1)d] \dots n \text{ times.}$$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore 2S_n = n [2a + (n-1)d] $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}} = \frac{n}{2} [2a + (n-1)d] \quad \text{or} \quad \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}} = na + \frac{n(n-1)}{2} d $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Ex. Let's find the sum of first 100 terms of A.P. 14, 16, 18, . . . .

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ Sum of first 100 terms of given A.P. is 11,300

blocks.label: Infobox
blocks.text:
Let's remember!
For the given Arithmetic Progression, if first term is $a$ and common
diffrence is $d$ then
$$t_n = [a+(n-1)d]$$
$$S_n = \frac{n}{2} [2a+(n-1)d] = na + \frac{n(n-1)}{2} d$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Let's find one more formula for sum of first $n$ terms.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: In the A.P. $a, a + d, a + 2d, a + 3d, \dots a + (n - 1)d$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: First term $= t_1 = a$ and $n^{\text{th}}$ term is $[a + (n - 1)d]$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \text{Now } S_n = \frac{n}{2} \left[ \underline{a} + \underline{a} + (n-1)d \right] $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore \quad S_n = \frac{n}{2} [t_1 + t_n] = \frac{n}{2} \text{ [First term+ last term]} $$

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Solved examples

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Ex. (1) Find the sum of first $n$ natural numbers.
Solution : First $n$ natural numbers are $1, 2, 3, \dots, n$.
Here $a = 1$, $d = 1$, $n^{\text{th}}$ term $= n$
$\therefore \text{S}_{\text{n}} = 1 + 2 + 3 + \dots + n$
$\text{S}_{\text{n}} = \frac{n}{2} [\text{First term+} \text{ last term}] \dots \dots \text{ (by the formula)}$
$= \frac{n}{2} [1 + n]$
$= \frac{n(n+1)}{2}$
$\therefore$ Sum of first $n$ natural number is $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ .

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Ex. (2) Find the sum of first $n$ even natural numbers.

Solution : First $n$ even natural numbers are $2, 4, 6, 8, \dots, 2n$.

$t_1 =$ First term $= 2$, $t_n =$ last term $= 2n$

Method I
$= \frac{n}{2} [t_1 + t_n]$
$= \frac{n}{2} [2 + 2n]$
$= \frac{n}{2} \times 2 (1 + n)$
$= n (1 + n)$

Method II
$S_n = 2 + 4 + 6 \dots + 2n$
$= 2(1 + 2 + 3 + \dots + n)$
$= \frac{2[n(n+1)]}{2}$
$= n (1 + n)$

Method III
$S_n = \frac{n}{2} [2a + (n-1)d]$
$= \frac{n}{2} [2 \times 2 + (n-1)2]$
$= \frac{n}{2} [4 + 2n - 2]$
$= \frac{n}{2} [2 + 2n]$
$= \frac{n}{2} \times 2 (1 + n)$
$= n (1 + n)$

$\therefore$ Sum of first $n$ even natural numbers is $n (1 + n)$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ Sum of first $n$ even natural numbers is $n (1+ n)$.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text: Ex. (3) Find the sum of first $n$ odd natural numbers.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Ex. (3) Find the sum of first $n$ odd natural numbers.

Solution : First $n$ natural numbers

$$1, 3, 5, 7, \dots, (2n-1).$$

$$a = t_1 = 1 \text{ and } t_n = (2n-1), d = 2$$

Method I
$$S_n = \frac{n}{2} [t_1 + t_n]$$
$$= \frac{n}{2} [1 + (2n-1)]$$
$$= \frac{n}{2} [1 + 2n - 1]$$
$$= \frac{n}{2} \times 2n$$
$$= n^2$$

Method II
$$S_n = \frac{n}{2} [2a + (n-1)d]$$
$$= \frac{n}{2} [2 \times 1 + (n-1) \times 2]$$
$$= \frac{n}{2} [2 + 2n - 2]$$
$$= \frac{n}{2} \times 2n$$
$$= n^2$$

Method III
$$1 + 3 + \dots 2n-1$$
$$= (1 + 2 + 3 + \dots + 2n)$$
$$- (2 + 4 + 6 + \dots + 2n)$$
$$= \frac{2n(2n+1)}{2} - \frac{2n(n+1)}{2}$$
$$= (2n^2 + n) - (n^2 + n)$$
$$= n^2$$

blocks.text:
Ex. (1) A mixer manufacturing company manufactured 600 mixers in $3^{\text{rd}}$ year and in
$7^{\text{th}}$ year they manufactured 700 mixers. If every year there is same growth in the
production of mixers then find (i) Production in the first year (ii) Production in
$10^{\text{th}}$ year (iii) Total production in first seven years.
Solution : Addition in the number of mixers manufactured by the company per year
is constant therefore the number of production in successive years is in A.P.
(i) Let's assume that company manufactured $\text{t}_{\text{n}}$ mixers in the $n^{\text{th}}$ year then as per
given information,
$\text{t}_3 = 600, \text{t}_7 = 700$
We know that $\text{t}_{\text{n}} = a + (n-1)d$
$\text{t}_3 = a + (3-1)d$
$a + 2d = 600. . . \text{ (I)}$
$\text{t}_7 = a + (7-1)d$
$\text{t}_7 = a + 6d = 700$
$a + 2d = 600 \therefore \text{Substituting } a = 600 - 2d \text{ in equation (II),}$
$600 - 2d + 6d = 700$
$4d = 100 \quad \therefore d = 25$
$a + 2d = 600 \quad \therefore a + 2 \times 25 = 600$
$a + 50 = 600 \quad \therefore a = 550$
$\therefore \text{ Production in first year was 550.}$
(ii) $\text{t}_{\text{n}} = a + (n-1)d$
$\text{t}_{10} = 550 + (10-1) \times 25$
$= 550 + 225$
Production in $10^{\text{th}}$ year was 775.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Production in $10^{\text{th}}$ year was 775.

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
(iii) For finding total production in first 7 years let's use formula for $S_n$.
$$S_n = \frac{n}{2} [2a+(n-1)d]$$
$$S_n = \frac{7}{2} [1100 + 150] = \frac{7}{2} [1250] = 7 \times 625 = 4375$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Total production in first 7 years is 4375 mixers.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
Ex. (2) Ajay sharma repays the borrowed amount of ₹ 3,25,000 by paying ₹ 30500
in the first month and then decreases the payment by ₹ 1500 every month. How
long will it take to clear his amount?

blocks.label: Answer
blocks.text:
Solution : Let the time required to clear the amount be $n$ months. The monthly payment
decreases by ₹ 1500. Therefore the payments are in A.P.

First term $= a = 30500, d = -1500$

Amount $= \text{S}_{\text{n}} = 3,25,000$

$\text{S}_{\text{n}} = \frac{n}{2} [2a + (n-1)d]$

$3,25,000 = \frac{n}{2} [2 \times 30500 + (n-1)d]$

$= \frac{n}{2} [2 \times 30500 - 1500n + 1500]$

$3,25,000 = 30500n - 750n^2 + 750n$

$\therefore 750n^2 - 31250n + 325000 = 0$

divide both sides by 250.

$\therefore 3n^2 - 125n + 1300 = 0$

$\therefore 3n^2 - 60n - 65n + 1300 = 0$

$\therefore 3n(n-20) - 65 (n-20) = 0$

$\therefore (n - 20) (3n - 65) = 0$

$\therefore n - 20 = 0 , 3n - 65 = 0$

$\therefore n = 20 \text{ or } n = \frac{65}{3} = 21\frac{2}{3}$

In an A.P. $n$ is a natural number.

$\therefore \quad n \neq \frac{65}{3} \quad \therefore \quad n = 20$

(Or, after 20 months, $\text{S}_{20} = 3,25,000$ then the total amount will be repaid. It is not
required to think about further period of time.)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ To clear the amount 20 months are needed.

a half circle $\text{P}_2$ of radius 1 cm which is on the
other side of the line.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Now again taking A as centre draw a half circle
$\text{P}_3$ of radius 1.5 cm. If we draw half
circles like this having radius 0.5 cm, 1 cm,
1.5 cm, 2 cm, we get a figure of spiral shape.
Find the length of such spiral shaped figure
formed by 13 such half circles. ($\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ )

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Solution : Semi circumferences $\mathrm{P}_1, \mathrm{P}_2, \mathrm{P}_3, \dots$ are drawn by taking centres A, B, A,
B,... It is given that radius of the first circle is $0.5 \mathrm{~cm}$. The radius of the second
circle is $1.0 \mathrm{~cm}, \ldots$ From this information we will find $\mathrm{P}_1, \mathrm{P}_2, \mathrm{P}_3, \dots \mathrm{P}_3$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Length of the first semi circumference $= \mathrm{P}_{1}=\pi \mathrm{r}_{1}=\pi \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \mathrm{P}_2 = \pi \mathrm{r}_2 = \pi \times 1 = \pi $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$P_3 = \pi r_3 = \pi \times 1.5 = \frac{3}{2} \pi$$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
The lengths are $\mathrm{P}_1, \mathrm{P}_2, \mathrm{P}_3, \dots$, and the numbers $\frac{1}{2} \pi, 1 \pi, \frac{3}{2} \pi, \dots$ are in A.P.
Here $a = \frac{1}{2} \pi, d = \frac{1}{2} \pi$, From this let's find $\mathrm{S}_{13}$.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ The total length of spiral shape formed by 13 semicircles is 143 cm.

Year First Year (2015) Second Year (2016) Third Year (2017) ...

$$a = 1,80,000 \quad d = 10,000 \quad n = ? \quad t_n = 2,50,000 \text{ ₹}$$ $$t_n = a + (n-1)d$$ $$2,50,000 = 1,80,000 + (n-1) \times 10,000$$ $$(n-1) \times 10000 = 70,000$$ $$(n-1) = 7$$ $$n = 8$$ In the $8^{\text{th}}$ year her annual salary will be ₹ 2,50,000.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex.** (1) Arati Gas Agency supplied LPG cylinder to the consumer for taxable
value of ₹ 545. GST charged is 5%. What is the amount of CGST and
SGST in the tax invoice ? What is the total amount paid by the consumer ?
Find the amount of GST to be paid by Arati Gas Agency.

blocks.label: Answer
blocks.text:
**Solution :** Rate of GST $= 5\%$ $\therefore$ Rate of CGST $2.5\%$, and Rate of SGST $= 2.5\%$.

$$ \text{CGST} = \frac{2.5}{100} \times 545 = 13.625 = \text{₹} \ 13.63 $$

$\therefore \text{SGST} = \text{CGST} = \text{₹} \ 13.63$

Amount paid by the consumer $= \text{Taxable value} + \text{CGST} + \text{SGST}$

$= 545 + 13.63 + 13.63$

$= 572.26$

Arati Gas Agency has to pay CGST $= \text{₹} \ 13.63.$ and SGST $= \text{₹} \ 13.63$

$\therefore$ Total GST to be paid $= 13.63 \times 2 = \text{₹} \ 27.26.$

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex.** (2) Courier service agent charged total ₹ 590 to courier a parcel from Na-
shik to Nagpur. In the tax invoice taxable value is ₹ 500 on which CGST
is ₹ 45 and SGST is ₹ 45. Find the rate of GST charged for this service.

**Solution** : Total GST = CGST + SGST = 45 + 45 = ₹ 90.

Rate of GST = $\frac{90}{500} \times 100 = 18\%$

$\therefore$ Rate of GST charged by agent is 18%.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex.** (3) Shreekar bought a Laptop with $10\%$ discount on printed price. The
printed price of that Laptop was $\text{\text{\text{\text️}$ } 50,000. $18\%$ GST was charged on dis-
counted price. Find the amount of CGST and SGST. What amount did
Shreekar pay ?

**Solution :** Discount $= 10\%$ of $50,000 = \text{\text{\text{\text{\text️}$ } 5,000}$

$\therefore$ Taxable value of Laptop $= 50,000 - 5,000 = \text{\text{\text{\text{\text{\text️}$ } 45,000.}$

$\therefore$ Rate of GST $= 18\%$ (Given) $\quad \therefore$ Rate of CGST $= 9\%$

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: What is Input Tax Credit ? (ITC)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
GST is levied and collected at every stage of trading from manufacturer to
consumer. When trader pays GST at the time of purchase, it is called '**Input**
**tax'** and he collects GST at the time of sale which is called '**Output tax'**.
At the time of paying GST to the government a trader deducts the input tax
from the output tax and pays the remaining tax. This deduction of input tax
is called **Input Tax Credit**.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: GST payable = Output tax - ITC

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In short, while paying taxes to the government each trader in the trading chain
subtracts the tax paid at the time of purchase from the tax collected at the time
of sale and pays the remaining tax.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Solved Examples 333

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (1)** Mr. Rohit is a retailer. He paid GST of ₹ 6500 at the time of purchase. He
collected GST of ₹ 8000 at the time of sale. (i) Find his input tax and out put tax.
(ii) What is his Input tax credit ? (iii) Find his payable GST. (iv) Hence find the
payable CGST and payable SGST.
**Solution** : Mr. Rohit's payable GST means, GST to be paid to the government by
Mr. Rohit.
(i) Output tax (tax collected at the time of sale) = ₹ 8000.
(ii) Input tax (tax paid at the time of purchase) = ₹ 6500
$\therefore$ ITC = ₹ 6500.
(iii) GST payable = Output tax - ITC
= ₹ 8000 - ₹ 6500 = ₹1500
(iv) $\therefore$ payable CGST = $\frac{1500}{2}$ = ₹ 750 and payable SGST = ₹ 750.

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (2)** M/s. Jay Chemicals purchased a liquid soap having taxable value $₹$ 8000 and
sold it to the consumers for the taxable value $₹$ 10,000. Rate of GST is 18%. Find
the CGST and SGST payable by M/s. Jay Chemicals.

**Solution :**

Input Tax = 18% of 8000
$$= \frac{18}{100} \times 8000 = ₹ 1440.$$
Output Tax = 18% of 10,000
$$= \frac{18}{100} \times 10000 = ₹ 1800$$
$\therefore$ GST payable = Output tax - ITC
$$= 1800 - 1440$$
$$= ₹ 360$$

$\therefore$ payable CGST = ₹ 180 and payable SGST = ₹ 180 by M/s. Jay Chemicals

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ payable CGST = ₹ 180 and payable SGST = ₹ 180 by M/s. Jay Chemicals

blocks.label: Solved-example
blocks.text:
**Ex. (3)** M/s. Jay Chemicals purchased a liquid soap for $₹$ 8000 (with GST) and sold it
to the consumers for $₹$ 10,000 (with GST). Rate of GST is 18%. Find the amount
of CGST and SGST to be paid by Jay Chemicals
**Solution** : Note that here the prices are including GST.

blocks.text: Total value (value with GST) = Taxable value + GST

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: If the taxable value of liquid soap is $₹$ 100, then the total value is $₹$ 118.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: The ratio of $\frac{\text{Total value}}{\text{Taxable Value}}$ is constant as the rate of GST is same.

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
i) For total value of ₹ 118, the taxable value is ₹ 100 and for total value of ₹ 8000,
let the taxable value be ₹ $x$ .

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \frac{x}{8000} = \frac{100}{118}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ \therefore x = \frac{8000}{118} \times 100 = \text{₹ } 6779.66 $$

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: $\therefore$ GST paid at the time of purchase $= 8000 - 6779.66$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: Input tax = ₹ 1220.34   $\therefore$ ITC = ₹ 1220.34 . . . . . (I)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: ii) For total value of $₹ 10,000$ let the taxable value be $₹ y$.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore \frac{y}{10000} = \frac{100}{118}$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore$ Output tax (tax collected) $= 10000.00 - 8474.58$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $$ = \text{₹} 1525.42 \dots \dots \text{ (II)} $$

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore$ GST payable = Output tax - Input tax = 1525.42 - 1220.34

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore$ payable CGST = payable SGST = 305.08 $\div$ 2 = ₹152.54

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Ans. : Jay Chemicals has to pay ₹ 152.54 CGST and ₹152.54 SGST.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Features of GST

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
$\bullet$ Many Indirect Taxes are subsumed under GST.
$\bullet$ No dispute between Goods and Services.
$\bullet$ Statewise Registration for traders.
$\bullet$ GSTIN holder needs to keep all the records and should pay GST in time.
$\bullet$ Transparency in transactions.
$\bullet$ This tax system is simple and easy to understand .
$\bullet$ Removal of cascading effect of taxes hence the prices are controlled
$\bullet$ Increase in Quality of Goods and Services as they are globally competetive.
$\bullet$ Boost to ‘Make in India’ project.
$\bullet$ Technology driven tax system leads to speedy decisions.
$\bullet$ Goods and Service Tax system is a Dual model, as equal amount of tax is levied
by Central and State governments.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Types of taxes under GST

blocks.label: List
blocks.text:
1. CGST-SGST (UTGST):
Tax levied for trading
within state (Intra state).

2. Composition Scheme : For
those GSTIN holders whose
annual turnover is between
20 lacs to 1.5 crore. They
pay CGST and SGST with
special rates.

3. IGST : Tax levied by central
government for Inter state
trading.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: For More Information

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: IGST- Integrated GST (for Inter state trade)

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
When trading of goods and services takes place between two or more states, the
GST is levied only by the Central Government, and it is termed as IGST, hence
the total amount is paid to the Central Government.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Suppose if a trader buys goods from another state and sells them in his state, then
let us see how he can avail of the ITC, which he has paid as IGST at the time of
purchase.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
**For example :** Trader 'M' (of Maharashtra) purchased scooter parts for ₹ 20,000
from trader 'P' (of Punjab) and paid tax of ₹ 5600 as IGST (GST rate 28%) to
the trader 'P'.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Trader 'M' sold these parts to local consumers for $₹$ 25,000 and collected $₹$ 7000
GST at the rate of 28%, bifurcated as CGST $₹$ 3500 + SGST $₹$ 3500

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
At the time of paying taxes to the Government, see, how to take ITC of
₹ 5600.

blocks.label: Infobox
blocks.text:
Note : For taking credit of IGST first preference to be given to pay the liability of
IGST then CGST and remaining amount can be utilised to pay SGST. Here there is
no IGST during the sale for trader 'M', so first the credit is used for CGST and then
for SGST.

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: CGST payable = 3500 - 3500 = 0 ₹

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
So out of ₹ 5600 credit of ₹ 3500 is utilised for CGST and the remaining amount
5600 - 3500 = 2100 is the credit available for SGST

blocks.label: Equation
blocks.text: $\therefore$ SGST payable = 3500 - 2100 = 1400 ₹

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Trader ‘M’ has to pay $\text{\rupee} 1400$ as SGST.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: Note that, trader ‘M’ got full credit of $5600$. (so that ITC is completely utilised)

In the previous class we have learnt the importance of savings and investments,
which you might have started practising whenever possible. We develop good habits
to maintain physical health, in the same way we should develop a habit of saving
and investing regularly to maintain financial health. There are many different ways

blocks.text: Shweta is working in a company. From this month her salary increased by $5\%$

also get bonus. She is thinking
of investing this increment. Her
friend Neha is working in the
office of a financial advisor,
so she can advise Shweta in
this matter. Neha told, ‘It is
important to have diversification
in one’s investments. e.g. you
should think of investing in
life insurance, health insurance,
owning a house, FD’s and
recurring account in the bank
etc...’ Shweta said, ‘I have
insurance and FD in the bank. Even Provident Fund is deducted regularly from
my salary. What are the other ways?’ Neha answered, “Investing in shares, Mutual
Funds (MF), Debentures, Bonds etc is more popular these days. Inclination of people
towards SIP is also increasing. Well I think, you are getting salary increment every
month, so Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) is suitable for you.”

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
We hear such dialogues every now and then. So we all must have the current
information beneficial for all as it says ‘बहुजन हिताय, बहुजन सुखाय’.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
In this chapter we shall learn about shares, mutual funds and SIP before
actually investing in them.

blocks.label: Sub-section-title
blocks.text: Let's learn.

blocks.label: Section-title
blocks.text: Shares

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
To own a shop is proprietorship. When two or more individuals coming together
to carry out a business is a partnership, which requires small capital. To establish
a company, desiring persons come together and form a company. Company is to
be registered under the Indian Companies' Act, 1956. Persons who form a company
are called Promoters and the company is called Limited Company.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Amount required to start a company is called **Capital**. This capital is divided into
small equal parts, each part is of ₹ 1, ₹ 2, ₹ 5, ₹ 10 or ₹ 100 etc. This small part is
called share of the company. These shares are sold in the sharemarket to raise the
capital.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
**Share** : A share is the smallest unit of the capital. The value of a share is printed
on the company's certificate with other details and it is called a share certificate.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
{\bf Share Holder} : A person who owns the share is called a share holder. The
shareholder is a part owner of the company in the proportion of number of shares
he/she holds.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
**Stock Exchange** : It is a place where buying and selling of shares take place. It
is also known as share market or stock market, equity market or capital market.
Companies should be listed in the stock market for trading.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Face Value (FV) : The value printed on the share certificate is called the
Face value of the share. It is also called Nominal value or Printed value or
par value.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
Market Value (MV) : The price at which the shares are sold or purchased in
the stock market is called Market value (MV) of the share.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text: In the live sharemarket the Market Value changes frequently.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
If the company's performance is better than expected, then those shares
are in demand. The number of shares is fixed, therefore share supply could not
be increased and hence the share price increases. If the company is not doing
well, the share price falls. [Increase in price is shown by $\blacktriangle$ (green triangle
upward), and decrease in price is shown by $\searrow$ (Red triangle downward).]
This is the reason for increase or decrease in SENSEX and NIFTY index.

blocks.label: Paragraph
blocks.text:
**Dividend** : The part of annual profit of a company which is distributed per
share among shareholders is called dividend. If the company is performing
well then the value of share capital increases hence the price of the share goes
up. As a result company gives good devidend. For the sharehlders the devidend
income is taxfree.

blocks.label: Infobox
blocks.text:
Let's remember!
Whatever may be the market value, the dividend is always reckoned on
the Face Value of a share.

blocks.label: Infobox
blocks.text:
**For more Information :**
There are two main stock exchanges, of India, BSE (Bombay Stock
Exchange) and NSE (National Stock Exchange). BSE is the oldest in
Asia while NSE is the India's largest stock Exchange.
There are two share indices namely - SENSEX and NIFTY which reflect
the overall market sentiments. SENSEX is SENSitive + indEX. Which was
introduced by BSE on 1-1-1986. SENSEX is detemined from 30 stocks.
They are the stocks of well established and financially sound companies
from the main sectors.
NIFTY as the name suggests is made up of two words that is NSE
and FIFTY which was introduced by NSE. It depends on India's topmost
outperforming 50 companies.

see two strips continuously flashing advances and declines in the market
value of shares. Generally the upper strip shows BSE shares while lower
strip shows NSE shares. Also find out what is the book value of shares

(1) If MV $> \text{FV}$ then the share is at premium.
(2) If $\text{MV} = \text{FV}$ then the share is at par.
(3) If $\text{MV} < \text{FV}$ then the share is at discount.
